Module 5 — Visual, Video, and Deepfake Verification
In contemporary digital journalism, misleading information increasingly circulates through manipulated images, edited videos, synthetic media, and AI-generated deepfakes that can appear highly realistic and emotionally persuasive.

This module develops the practical visual verification skills needed to investigate images, videos, and multimodal digital content in AI-driven information environments. Learners explore reverse image search workflows, metadata interpretation, keyframe extraction, geolocation techniques, and deepfake detection strategies while analyzing how visual manipulation influences public perception and online virality.

The module emphasizes critical visual analysis, contextual verification, and human editorial judgment as essential components of trustworthy digital journalism.
1
Deepfake Detection Checklist
This interactive checklist presents seven common visual and temporal artifacts associated with deepfakes (e.g., unnatural blinking, inconsistent lighting, lip‑sync mismatch). Learners tick the warning signs they observe in a hypothetical video. After submitting, they receive a risk assessment (low/medium/high) based on how many indicators were selected.
Learning outcome: Learners internalise a structured set of red flags for rapid deepfake assessment and understand that multiple indicators increase suspicion.
Deepfake detection checklist | Module 5

🕵️ Deepfake detection checklist

Use this interactive checklist to assess whether a video might be AI‑generated. Check each warning sign you observe.
2
Keyframe Investigation Exercises
Three multiple‑choice questions test learners’ understanding of keyframe extraction – why it is essential for video verification, which tools are used (e.g., InVID/WeVerify), and what to do with extracted keyframes (reverse image search). Each answer is followed by a brief explanation that reinforces the workflow.
Learning outcome: Learners grasp the concept of keyframes, know the standard tool for extraction, and understand the correct next step for verifying video authenticity.
Keyframe investigation | Module 5

🎞️ Keyframe investigation exercises

Extracting keyframes is the first step in video verification. Test your knowledge.

Images and videos often spread faster and generate stronger emotional reactions than textual information. At the same time, AI-generated synthetic media and deepfake technologies are making visual manipulation increasingly difficult to detect.

This module helps learners develop the visual verification mindset and technical investigation skills necessary to identify manipulated media, evaluate visual credibility, and respond responsibly to synthetic content in modern digital journalism.
3
Image Verification Challenges
Three realistic image‑verification scenarios are presented, each with a short description and a question. Learners choose the best first step or most likely conclusion from four options. Scenarios cover shadow‑angle verification (SunCalc), detection of AI‑smoothing artifacts, and using visual clues (logos) for geolocation when metadata is absent.
Learning outcome: Learners learn to prioritise verification techniques based on the type of visual content and to recognise common telltale signs of manipulation.
Image verification challenges | Module 5

📸 Image verification challenges

Test your ability to spot visual inconsistencies and choose the correct verification method.

1818 Magazine by Stephanie Toole
4
Metadata Analysis Simulations
Two simulated metadata extracts (EXIF data) are shown for a photo and an aerial image. Learners answer questions about suspicious inconsistencies (e.g., Photoshop modification one day after capture) and about the meaning of missing GPS data. Immediate feedback explains correct interpretations and warns against over‑reliance on any single metadata field.
Learning outcome: Learners become able to read and interpret basic EXIF metadata, identify red flags (e.g., post‑capture editing), and understand that missing GPS is not proof of a fake.

📷 Metadata analysis simulations

❓ What is the most concerning red flag in this metadata?
📄 File: disaster_aerial.jpg
🕒 Date/Time Original: 2025-02-10 09:15:00
📍 GPS: not present
📷 Camera: DJI Mavic 3 (drone)
✏️ Software: unknown
❓ What can you conclude from the missing GPS data?
After completing this module, learners will be able to critically investigate visual and video-based information, identify synthetic media risks, and apply professional verification workflows to images, videos, and AI-generated content in contemporary newsroom environments.
5
Interactive Visual Comparison Tasks
Two side‑by‑side visual comparisons are presented. In the first, learners compare two simulated images – one with shadow inconsistencies and duplicate pixel patterns, the other consistent. In the second, a description of a portrait with mismatched lighting is given. Learners decide whether the image is authentic, a composite, or AI‑generated. Each choice triggers explanatory feedback on manipulation indicators.
Learning outcome: Learners practice spotting lighting inconsistencies, copy‑paste artifacts, and composite boundaries – essential skills for detecting manipulated or AI‑synthesised visuals.
Visual comparison tasks | Module 5

🖼️ Interactive visual comparison tasks

Two similar images – one authentic, one manipulated. Identify the manipulated one and explain your reasoning.

📸 Image A (simulated)
🔍 Possible manipulation
Image A: The building's shadow direction does not match the sun position. Two people have identical pixel patterns (copy‑paste).
📸 Image B (simulated)
✅ Consistent metadata
Image B: Shadows are consistent; no duplicate elements; EXIF data matches camera settings.
❓ Which image is most likely manipulated?
🔍 Second comparison: Lighting anomalies

Photo of a person in front of a landscape: the face is brightly lit from the left, but the background shows shadows pointing right (light from the right).

Throughout the module, learners will engage with practical visual verification activities, including:
  • deepfake detection simulations
  • image comparison tasks
  • metadata investigation exercises
  • video keyframe analysis
  • geolocation workflows
  • newsroom-inspired multimodal verification scenarios
